newsitem.title: USA: U.S. attacks Iraq with cruise missiles.
newsitem.headline: U.S. attacks Iraq with cruise missiles.

text.p: The U.S. military on Tuesday launched cruise missile strikes against air defence targets in southern Iraq in retaliation for Iraqi military attacks against Kurds in the north, defence officials said.

The Pentagon announced only that the unmanned cruise missiles were fired at "selected air defence targets in Iraq," but defence officials said they were fired from U.S. warships in the Gulf and by at least one B-52 bomber against air defence and command and control targets in southern Iraq.

The officials, who asked not to be identified, said missiles were apparently not fired at military targets in and around Baghdad, although reports from the capital said air raid sirens had blared there.
The defence officials said several dozen of the highly accurate missiles were launched at radars, missile sites and command and control facilities in the raid, which lasted about an hour.
No further details were given in the Pentagon's formal announcement issued at 2 a.m. EDT (0600 GMT), which was about 10 a.m. in Baghdad.

It said President Bill Clinton ordered the strikes and that he planned to make a formal announcement at the White House at about 8 a.m. EDT (1200 GMT). That was to be followed with a news conference by Defence Secretary William Perry.

In Baghdad, residents said air raid sirens had blared in parts of the Iraqi capital on Tuesday but were not heard all over the city. Witnesses said anti-aircraft fire was launched from positions in Baghdad, but it was not immediately clear what the fire was aimed at.
An Iraqi television channel run by President Saddam Hussein's son Uday confirmed on Tuesday the U.S. military strikes against Iraq.
U.S. officials said on Monday night that Saddam must be made to pay for ignoring U.S. warnings and launching weekend attacks against Kurds north of the 36th parallel in his country.

"At the direction of the president, the Department of Defence has launched cruise missiles to attack selected air defence targets in Iraq. No further details are available at this time," Tuesday's brief Pentagon announcement said.

"The president plans to make a formal statement on this operation at approximately 8 a.m. this morning. Shortly after the president makes his statement, the secretary of defence and the vice chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff will hold a press conference" at the Pentagon, it added.

The United States had stationed warships armed with accurate Tomahawk cruise missiles in the Gulf and moved B-52 bombers carrying air-launched cruise missiles to Guam in the Pacific. The B-52s can fly non-stop into missile range several hundred miles from Iraq.
The $1.2 million ship-launched Tomahawks can fly unmanned nearly 700 miles (1,120 km) and strike targets with high accuracy.

The White House believes Saddam sent three tank divisions composed of 30,000-40,000 elite Republican Guard troops into northern Iraq over the weekend to help a Kurdish faction involved in a bloody power struggle with another Kurdish group with links to Iran.
It says U.N. Security Council resolutions approved after a U.S.-led coalition defeated Iraq in the 1991 Gulf War provide the legal basis for responding to Saddam's actions.

White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters in Milwaukee on Sunday during a Clinton campaign appearance that there was evidence some of the Iraqi forces that overran the Kurdish stronghold of Arbil over the weekend were "penetrating deeper" into northern Iraq.
The State Department on Monday night urged all American citizens to leave Iraq, citing "soaring violence" in the north and Baghdad's "renewed campaign of repression."

"The U.S. government views with grave concern the latest reports of soaring violence in northern Iraq. Given the government of Iraq's renewed campaign of repression, it is strongly recommended that all U.S. citizens leave Iraq," the department said.
In 1993 Clinton launched a cruise missile attack on Iraq in response to its alleged plot to assassinate former President George Bush while Bush was visiting Kuwait that year.
The missiles destroyed an Iraqi intelligence headquarters in central Baghdad where U.S. officials said the plot had been hatched.
